evaluation.positioning_hook: A teleporting father races through downtown Los Angeles to rescue his kidnapped daughter before a black-ops team collars her powers and forces a deadly blind jump.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The rescue engine is immediate, emotional, and easy to sell: a father, a kidnapped child, and a ticking-clock chase with a sci-fi power twist. The appeal is strongest for genre buyers and action-thriller audiences rather than a broad four-quadrant crowd, because the script is built around a very specific premise and a contained emotional relationship.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands in the first pages: James teleports, uses a mysterious black app to locate Rosie, and has to coordinate a rescue through a phone call while the enemy watches her in real time. The rules of the power and the rescue objective are clear early, which gives the script a clean, pitchable engine.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: James has a strong core want and a clear emotional wound around Rosie and her mother, but he is mostly defined by mission pressure and protective urgency. Rosie is vivid and sympathetic, and Nora/Edgar/Davidson add texture, though the script is more built on function than on deep character surprise.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The phone-based rescue choreography, the clapping code with a trapped child, and the physics of blind-jumping give the script a fresh action set-up. It is still operating in a familiar kidnapped-child/black-ops lane, but the execution has enough specificity to feel ownable.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The script is relentlessly forward-moving: every beat either advances the rescue, tightens the surveillance net, or escalates the danger of the jump. The final airborne sequence is especially strong because it converts the premise into a literal life-or-death countdown with no room to stall.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The central idea is simple enough to grasp instantly, but the combination of teleportation, a child prisoner, and a live remote rescue gives it a memorable shape. It feels fresh without being abstract, though the underlying structure still sits close to familiar pursuit-thriller DNA.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The world has useful tactical details — ceramic comm chips, collars that block powers, silent surveillance, A/B teams, and the black app — but it is mostly a pressure container for the rescue. The office-building setting and black-site infrastructure are specific, yet the script does not build a larger social or institutional world beyond the immediate chase.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The tone is tense and kinetic, but what makes it stand out is the collision of brutal tactical menace with a father-daughter emotional plea. The script keeps that register consistent, especially in the clapping communication and the final sky-fall sequence, which gives it a distinct emotional-action blend.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: There are seeds of deeper backstory — the mother’s death, Edgar’s family tie, Davidson’s control, and the ethics of using a child’s powers — but the script stays focused on the immediate rescue. It is effective as a contained feature premise, though it does not suggest a lot of hidden layers beyond the central mission.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: James and Rosie are the engine, and their call-and-response dynamic is the script’s strongest relationship. Nora, Davidson, and Edgar create a workable antagonist triangle, but the story is not built for broad ensemble interplay; it lives primarily on the father-daughter bond and the pressure it creates.

lead_characters.name: James
lead_characters.demographics: Male, 30s, father, physically capable, contemporary American.
lead_characters.hook: An exhausted but highly competent everyman with teleportation powers, James is operating on pure paternal panic and tactical instinct. He’s funny only in the way desperate people get funny, and the script gives him a hard edge when he realizes the people holding Rosie are not negotiating in good faith; his love for his daughter is the only thing keeping him from becoming fully feral.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Tom Hardy in Locke or Michael Shannon in Take Shelter — a contained, high-pressure role where the actor carries the movie through urgency, guilt, and physical command. It gives a performer the chance to play action, grief, and moral fury in one sustained rescue run.

lead_characters.name: Rosie
lead_characters.hook: Rosie is the emotional center of the script: frightened, obedient, and trying very hard to be a good kid in a situation she barely understands. Her power is enormous, but the writing makes the real drama her terror of using it and her longing for her mother, which gives the character heartbreaking innocence under extreme pressure.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of child role that can define a young performer the way Brooklynn Prince in The Florida Project did — emotionally precise, vulnerable, and unforgettable without being cute. It offers a rare chance for a child actor to carry fear, confusion, and courage in the same role.

lead_characters.name: Nora
lead_characters.hook: Nora is the cold, efficient face of the operation, the kind of antagonist who understands procedure and uses it as cruelty. She reads as disciplined rather than cartoonish, which makes her more dangerous in the room because she believes she is doing the right thing.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is strong antagonist material in the vein of Rebecca Ferguson in Mission: Impossible or Jodie Comer in The Last Duel — controlled, intelligent, and physically alert. It gives an actor a chance to play authority, menace, and tactical intelligence without losing composure.

lead_characters.name: Davidson
lead_characters.hook: Davidson is the polished institutional predator: calm, managerial, and willing to let other people absorb the violence. He has the most overtly cynical worldview in the script, and the fact that he can speak in civilized language while ordering a child collaring makes him the story’s most chilling power figure.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actor the same pleasure as Bryan Cranston in Trumbo or Michael Keaton in Spotlight — authority, intelligence, and a moral rot that can be played with restraint. It’s a delicious villain part for a performer who can make control feel threatening.

lead_characters.name: Edgar
lead_characters.hook: Edgar is the internal fracture in the enemy side: physically dangerous, emotionally compromised, and tied to Rosie by blood. He starts as a tactical presence and then becomes the script’s pressure valve, because his loyalty is split between the operation and the child.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that lets an actor do the turn-and-release work of a Jon Bernthal or Yahya Abdul-Mateen II part — controlled menace that can break into action and emotion fast. The family tie gives the performance a personal stake that lifts it above standard henchman territory.

casting_characteristics: one child lead carrying sustained fear and dialogue
one physically capable adult lead with action and emotional range
one athletic supporting antagonist with fight ability

notable_requirements: office building lobby and upper floors

technical.vfx_details: Teleportation blips, electric bursts, falling-from-sky shots, and a few perspective-driven effects for the blind-jump sequence.
technical.sfx_needs: collar effects, electrical discharge, rubber-bullet impacts, practical fight beats, and death-by-wall impact staging.

platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model: contained genre thriller with a strong hook for streamer launch or specialty theatrical play.

budget.note: Contemporary locations keep the footprint contained, but the rooftop work, sky-fall sequence, teleportation effects, and action beats will push beyond a simple contained-thriller cost profile.

casting.note: The lead needs to carry action, guilt, and paternal panic at once, while Rosie has to sustain fear and clarity through a large share of the emotional engine. Edgar also needs credible fight ability, which narrows the supporting cast pool.

development.note: The premise is clean and the rescue objective is clear from page one; the main development conversation is packaging and execution scale rather than story comprehension.

comp_set.title: Upgrade
comp_set.why_it_comps: Shares the body-control sci-fi premise and lean, propulsive revenge energy, with a protagonist whose powers are inseparable from physical vulnerability.

comp_set.title: Run Lola Run
comp_set.why_it_comps: Matches the breathless, clock-ticking momentum and the sense of a single urgent mission driving every scene.

comp_set.title: Source Code
comp_set.why_it_comps: Comps on the clean high-concept mechanics and the way a contained mission becomes emotionally legible through a single relationship.

comp_set.title: The Invisible Man
comp_set.why_it_comps: Shares the modern, stripped-down genre packaging and the feeling of a protagonist fighting an unseen, technologically enabled threat.

audience_target.primary_audience: Genre audiences who want a fast, emotional rescue thriller with a sci-fi twist and a strong parent-child hook.
audience_target.demographics: Adults 18-49, with a slight male skew for the action mechanics and strong female reach through the child-endangerment/family stakes.

budget_tier.note: Contemporary Los Angeles locations, a small cast, and limited set count keep it indie, with moderate VFX and action sequences as the main cost drivers.

types_of_buyers: streamer originals dev execs building genre-forward feature slates
boutique genre financiers looking for a contained hook
specialty distributors seeking a high-concept action title
producer-directors with a strong visual reel and limited-budget action experience
lane_fit.detail: The script sits in the lane of smart, contained genre pieces that can be sold on premise and executed without tentpole scale. The father-daughter emotional spine gives it enough heart to widen beyond pure effects-driven sci-fi.

ip_potential.detail: Standalone feature: the premise is built around one rescue mission and one family relationship, with no clear spinoff vector beyond this story.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The rescue engine is instantly legible.
strengths.what_it_means: That clarity makes the script easy to pitch, easy to market, and easy for a buyer to understand in one pass. It gives the project a clean commercial spine for streamer or specialty theatrical packaging.
strengths.evidence: James teleports through downtown, calls Rosie through the black app, and learns in real time that she is being watched and moved toward a collar.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The father-daughter call is the movie.
strengths.what_it_means: The emotional hook is not decorative; it is the delivery system for the action, which makes the premise feel human rather than gadget-driven. That is exactly the kind of built-in audience attachment that helps a genre script travel beyond effects buyers.
strengths.evidence: The clapping code, the repeated pleas for Mommy, and James coaching Rosie through fear all turn the rescue into a relationship test.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The blind-jump finale is a strong set piece.
strengths.what_it_means: The climax converts the premise into a visually memorable, high-stakes action sequence that can sell the trailer and justify the genre promise. It gives the project a signature moment that feels specific rather than generic.
strengths.evidence: Rosie repeatedly blips upward and falls through the sky while James times the rotation to catch her and reverse the fall.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The power rules are simple and playable.
strengths.what_it_means: Clear rules reduce audience friction and make the action readable, which is a major advantage for a contained sci-fi thriller. Buyers like premises where the mechanics can be explained fast and then paid off cleanly.
strengths.evidence: Teleportation works by line of sight or memory, and the collar blocks the power with a clear physical consequence.

whats_special.headline: This is a clean, high-concept rescue thriller with a built-in emotional engine: a father trying to save his kidnapped daughter through a live, tactical phone call. The contained contemporary footprint and modest cast make it packageable at indie scale, while the teleportation rules and sky-fall climax give buyers a trailer-ready genre hook.

items.area: The premise is strongest as a short-form engine.
items.detail: The script is built around one rescue run, one location network, and one climax, which is a very efficient feature premise but also a sign that the material is operating close to a short-film spine. For feature buyers, the question will be whether the 20-page version is enough story for a full commercial run time without feeling stretched.

items.area: Rosie carries the emotional burden very young.
items.detail: The child role is central to the movie’s emotional credibility, and the script asks a very young performer to sustain fear, confusion, obedience, and courage across the whole piece. That is a real casting conversation because the movie’s heart depends on a child actor landing a difficult tonal balance.

items.area: The action scale rises fast at the end.
items.detail: The rooftop capture, sky-fall sequence, and repeated blips in midair create a visual finish that is more expensive than the opening pages suggest. The project stays contemporary and contained, but the climax will still require disciplined effects and stunt planning to stay inside indie economics.

items.area: The antagonist side is functional, not deeply layered.
items.detail: Davidson, Nora, and the tactical teams do the job cleanly, but the script is not building a richly textured enemy world; it is building pressure. That keeps the momentum high, though it also means the movie’s long-tail appeal rests almost entirely on the central rescue concept and James-Rosie bond.

issues.headline: The main friction is scale: the script plays like a very efficient, very sellable rescue thriller, but it is also a compact piece that will need careful feature expansion and disciplined climax execution. The child lead and the airborne finale are the two conversations every buyer will have before saying yes.
